findings.description: An absent transcription runtime row returned SQL NULL, causing IF NOT checks to fall through at request admission and worker claim.
findings.correction: Both gate checks now use NOT COALESCE((SELECT enabled ...), false).

findings.description: After a transcript draft completed, disabling source clipping denied live_clip_get but transcription status still returned its draft text.

reproduced_before_fix.method: Isolated local PGlite case using the real deployed-schema fixture and new migration
reproduced_before_fix.result: Source clip RPC denied while status returned existing draft; no hosted calls

findings.correction: The transcription command read/modify boundary now requires live_streams.clip_can_read(c.id, uid), matching current source-read rights.
findings.regression_test: draft reads inherit clip-read revocation when source clipping is disabled

independent_regression_run.database: local PGlite; actual SQL functions and grants

security_observations: Connection handler derives actor and session from verified user authentication plus live_integration_context; body actor/session identifiers are rejected.
Credential tables have RLS and no ordinary-role grants; service-only RPC checks active publisher session on every operation; ordinary metadata contains no ciphertext or tokens.
OAuth state is a random secret stored as SHA-256, bound to actor/session/provider, expiring after ten minutes and atomically claimed once.
AES-GCM additional data binds encrypted token envelopes to actor, connection/state id and platform; no provider bodies are returned in errors.
Provider calls use fixed endpoints with redirects rejected and bounded bodies; account selection uses only provider-returned eligible accounts.
Disconnect clears local credentials and outstanding states; a stale refresh/completion cannot restore the disconnected connection. Provider-side revocation remains explicitly separate.
Transcription worker RPC checks current session, source rights, revision/path, moderation and copyright before claim/check/finish; private media grants are rechecked after signing.
Worker completion stores a timed caption draft; applying subtitles requires current authorized explicit review and the existing validated clip-edit transaction.

Browser callback binds sessionStorage state and owner, strips query before exchange, reuses one exchange promise under Strict Mode, validates provider navigation, and rejects late results after account change.
